questions.q: Why were the descendants of Dan looking for a territory in which to live?
questions.a: The descendants of Dan were looking for a territory in which to live because they had not been able to occupy all of the territory that had been assigned to them.

questions.q: What did the people of Dan want the Levite to ask God?
questions.a: The people of Dan wanted the Levite to ask God if they would succeed in what they were trying to do.

questions.q: What did the five men from Dan want to do with the land of Laish?
questions.a: The five men from Dan wanted to take possession of the land so their people could live there.

questions.q: What did the five men say was in the houses of Laish?
questions.a: The five men said that in the houses of Laish there were a sacred vest, household idols, and a silver molded figure.
Micah was angry because the Danites stole the idols he had made and his priest and they were leaving.

questions.q: Why did Micah turn and go back to his house?
questions.a: When Micah saw that they were too strong for him, he turned and went back to his house.

questions.q: Why was there no one to rescue the people of Laish?
questions.a: There was no one to rescue the people of Laish because it was a long way from Sidon and they had no other allies.

questions.q: Who were the priests for the tribe of the Danites?
questions.a: Jonathan, the son of Gershom, (the grandson of Moses) and his sons were priests for the tribe of Dan.

commentary.text: The Danites seek to enlarge their inheritance, and rob Micah.

—The Danites determined to take Micah's gods with them. Oh the folly of these Danites! How could they imagine those gods should protect them, that could not keep themselves from being stolen! To take them for their own use, was a double crime; it showed they neither feared God, nor regarded man, but were lost both to godliness and honesty. What a folly was it for Micah to call those his gods, which he had made, when He only is to be worshipped by us as God, that made us! That is put in God's place, which we are concerned about, as if our all were bound up in it. If people will walk in the name of their false gods, much more should we love and serve the true God!
